title: 236. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Exact versus Approximate Algebraic Solutions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the exact solution set of \(x^2=2\).
questions.question: Which option gives the exact solution set of \(x^2=2\)?
questions.explanation: Solving \(x^2=2\) gives \(x=\sqrt{2}\) or \(x=-\sqrt{2}\), so the exact solution set is \(x=\pm\sqrt{2}\). The decimal \(1.414\) is only an approximation of \(\sqrt{2}\) and is not exact.
questions.hint: When a square equals a non-perfect square, keep the radical form for the exact solution.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the exact solution set of \(2x^2-6=0\).
questions.question: Which option gives the exact solution set of \(2x^2-6=0\)?
questions.explanation: From \(2x^2-6=0\), we get \(2x^2=6\), so \(x^2=3\). Therefore the exact solutions are \(x=\pm\sqrt{3}\). The value \(1.732\) is only an approximation of \(\sqrt{3}\).
questions.hint: Isolate \(x^2\) first, then write the exact radical form.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the exact simplified form of \(\sqrt{50}\).
questions.question: Which option is the exact simplified form of \(\sqrt{50}\)?
questions.explanation:
Write \(50\) as \(25\cdot2\). Then
\[
\sqrt{50}=\sqrt{25\cdot2}=\sqrt{25}\sqrt{2}=5\sqrt{2}
\]
The decimal \(7.071\) is only an approximation of \(\sqrt{50}\), not the exact simplified form.
questions.hint: Look for the largest perfect-square factor of the radicand.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the exact solution set of \(x^2+4x+1=0\).
questions.question: Which option gives the exact solution set of \(x^2+4x+1=0\)?
questions.hint: Use the quadratic formula and simplify the radical exactly.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an exact solution from an approximate solution for \(x^2=7\).
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes exact and approximate solutions of \(x^2=7\)?

options.label: A
options.text: The exact solutions are \(x=\pm\sqrt{7}\), and approximate solutions are \(x\approx\pm2.65\).

options.label: B
options.text: The exact solutions are \(x=\pm2.65\), and approximate solutions are \(x\approx\pm\sqrt{7}\).

questions.explanation: Solving \(x^2=7\) exactly gives \(x=\pm\sqrt{7}\). Since \(\sqrt{7}\approx2.64575\), rounded to two decimal places the approximate solutions are \(x\approx\pm2.65\). Option B reverses the exact and approximate forms.
questions.hint: Exact solutions keep radicals; approximate solutions use rounded decimal values.

questions.concept: Exact solutions of simple quadratic equations
questions.learningObjective: Identify the exact solution set of \(2x^2-8=0\).
questions.question: Which option gives the exact solution set of \(2x^2-8=0\)?
questions.explanation: From \(2x^2-8=0\), we get \(2x^2=8\), so \(x^2=4\). Therefore the exact solutions are \(x=\pm2\). The decimal \(2.828\) is not relevant here because \(x^2=4\) has integer solutions.
questions.hint: Isolate \(x^2\), then determine whether the result is a perfect square.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the exact solution set of \(x^2=18\).
questions.question: Which option gives the exact solution set of \(x^2=18\)?
questions.explanation:
Since \(x^2=18\), \(x=\pm\sqrt{18}\). Simplify:
\[
\sqrt{18}=\sqrt{9\cdot2}=3\sqrt{2}
\]
Therefore the exact solution set is \(x=\pm3\sqrt{2}\). The value \(4.24\) is only an approximation.
questions.hint: Simplify the radical by factoring out the largest perfect square.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the exact solution set of \(x^2-6x+7=0\).
questions.question: Which option gives the exact solution set of \(x^2-6x+7=0\)?
questions.explanation:
Use the quadratic formula with \(a=1\), \(b=-6\), and \(c=7\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
x &= \frac{6\pm\sqrt{(-6)^2-4(1)(7)}}{2}\\
&= \frac{6\pm\sqrt{36-28}}{2}\\
&= \frac{6\pm\sqrt{8}}{2}\\
&= \frac{6\pm2\sqrt{2}}{2}\\
&= 3\pm\sqrt{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the exact solution set is \(x=3\pm\sqrt{2}\). The option \(3\pm\sqrt{3}\) comes from an incorrect discriminant.
questions.hint: Compute \(b^2-4ac\) first, then simplify the radical exactly.

questions.question: Which option gives the exact real solution of \(x^3=10\)?
questions.explanation: The exact real solution of \(x^3=10\) is \(x=\sqrt[3]{10}\). The decimal \(2.154\) is only an approximation of \(\sqrt[3]{10}\). Therefore the exact solution is option B.
questions.hint: Keep cube roots in radical form when an exact solution is required.
